status_summary: The administration has proposed cuts and consolidation and House committees have moved toward lower DOL spending and WIOA changes, but Congress has enacted none of it: the FY 2027 request would cut DOL discretionary spending to $10.7 billion from $13.3 billion (per DOL's Budget in Brief; Bloomberg Government reported $9.9 billion) and replace many WIOA Title I programs with a $3.4 billion Make America Skilled Again block grant, and the House Appropriations Committee advanced a FY 2027 Labor-HHS-Education bill 34-28 on 2026-06-09 that, per the committee's bill summary, funds DOL at $9.8 billion, 27 percent below FY 2026 enacted, while H.R. 8210, a WIOA reauthorization, cleared the House Education and Workforce Committee 19-14 on 2026-04-21. EO 14278 (signed 2025-04-23) ordered a review of federal workforce programs that could recommend consolidating or eliminating programs. DOL's 2025-05-29 pause of contractor-operated Job Corps centers was preliminarily enjoined in New York on 2025-06-25, and in a stipulated settlement filed 2026-08-10 in Cabrera v. Department of Labor (D.D.C.), not shown as entered by the court, DOL agreed to rescind the pause and termination notices. Public Law 119-103, signed 2026-09-02, continues FY 2026 Labor-HHS-Education funding through 2026-12-11, so full-year FY 2027 decisions remain open.

timeline.event: President signs EO 14278 (published 2025-04-28). Section 3 directs the Secretaries of Labor, Commerce and Education to review federal workforce programs within 90 days and recommend integrating systems, reforming or eliminating ineffective programs, and consolidating programs.

DOL announces it will begin shutting down contractor-operated Job Corps centers; EPI ties the move to a White House budget request that would eliminate Job Corps and cut DOL's workforce training budget by more than half in favor of a proposed state and local grant program.

After a temporary restraining order on 2025-06-04, a federal judge in the Southern District of New York (Judge Andrew Carter, per VTDigger) issues a preliminary injunction that keeps Job Corps centers open while litigation continues, finding DOL likely lacked authority to end a congressionally mandated program.

The administration's FY 2027 request, submitted to Congress on 2026-04-03, would cut DOL discretionary spending to $10.7 billion from $13.3 billion enacted for FY 2026 (DOL Budget in Brief; Bloomberg Government reported $9.9 billion), create a $3.425 billion Make America Skilled Again grant consolidating 12 workforce programs, eliminate Job Corps (with $176.4 million for closeout) and eliminate the Senior Community Service Employment Program.

Rep. Tim Walberg introduces the A Stronger Workforce for America Act of 2026 (H.R. 8210), a WIOA reauthorization whose text expands performance reporting; the House Education and Workforce Committee reports it 19-14 on 2026-04-21 (committee markup page), and no floor action was found.

Bloomberg Government reports (month only; the first of the month is used) that a House Appropriations package rejects the $3.4 billion Make America Skilled Again framework for the second year in a row, cuts Job Corps by almost $1 billion instead of eliminating it, allocates $5 million to registered apprenticeships, and closes OFCCP, the Women's Bureau and the Bureau of International Labor Affairs.

The full House Appropriations Committee advances its FY 2027 Labor-HHS-Education bill 34-28; the committee's bill summary funds DOL at $9.8 billion, $3.7 billion (27 percent) below FY 2026 enacted, with $290 million for apprenticeships. The reported bill (H.R. 9260, reported 2026-06-11) provides about $2.60 billion for Training and Employment Services and $880 million for Job Corps.
The House passes a continuing resolution (H.R. 9770) 220-205 that extends government funding through December 4, 2026; full-year FY 2027 appropriations bills remain unfinished.

In Cabrera v. Department of Labor (D.D.C., No. 25-1909), DOL and student plaintiffs file a stipulated settlement and dismissal under which DOL is to rescind its 2025-05-29 Job Corps pause and related termination notices and take no further action on them, with the case to be dismissed with prejudice after entry.
